touches.text: When a client's loopback dial to the proxy is refused (no socket on the box), the client wakes the proxy once through the bus (database start) and retries for up to 60 s. Any other failure, or a wake that fails, is raised at once and names why. WHY: the command lazy-inits the system (5.8.3.2.1), and after a reboot nothing else starts the proxy. - CC

Every box runs its own instance of the database proxy, and everything on that box talks only to it (4.3.1.5.1.4.1.1). Each box's proxy is its own instance (1.3.4), so this agrees with 5.5.3.8 ("a device runs on one box"): no instance is duplicated, the class has one instance per box, like the foundational set of 5.5.3.8.1. WHY: the local read is fast, and the cache it fills is every box's backup. -amm; the fit with 5.5.3.8 - akienasus_cc_0
It wakes the device when it's not running and is needed.
Publishes a client tool (connect, read, write, query ...) that talks to the database over its socket, no bus hop: faster (2.3.7.1.1).
The detect-and-start lives in one tool, the waker, and it sits inside connect: every client's connect is a wake attempt, so no caller can forget one. A probe watches and reports; the waker acts.
Its sockets dial only its own box's Postgres on loopback, never the inference host, so it stands on the sole-path allowed list (11.4.1, 17.13) beside web_operator and usage. - CC
